title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
key_facts: Meta has open sourced code that lets people build their own gadgets that run Muse, its new AI agent.
Meta suggests projects such as Muse on a colour E Ink display for reminders, on an HDMI stick to show Muse on a big screen, or on a small touchscreen device like a do-it-yourself Muse Charm.
Meta says builders can program an off-the-shelf ESP32 board or set up a Raspberry Pi with its SDKs, then connect Muse to displays, buttons, sensors and actuators.
Meta cautions builders to "Proceed at your own risk!".
Meta is also giving away a gadget it made, the Muse Home Link, which uses community-built skills to turn on a light, control a TV or send a document to a printer, depending on the setup.
Nat Friedman of Meta Superintelligence Labs says 5,000 of these gadgets were manufactured.
People can claim a waitlist spot now, with shipping due sometime this month (October 2026).
quote_evidence: Meta now lets you make your own Muse gadgets that feature the company’s new AI agent with code that the company open sourced.
It manufactured 5,000 of the gadgets, according to Meta Superintelligence Labs’ Nat Friedman, and you can claim a waitlist spot for the Muse Home Link now ahead of shipping sometime this month.
why_it_matters_hint: Builders can run Meta's Muse agent on their own hardware, and Meta is testing demand with 5,000 Home Link devices.
event_date: Not stated; The Verge published it on 2 Oct 2026.
notes: Short article (about 1,450 characters). Only The Verge read; all quotes are Meta's own words as relayed by The Verge. Shipping date for Home Link is only 'sometime this month'.
